sections.text_helper: Section 31.3.36 "ADC triggers" in chapter 31 (Advanced-control timers (TIM1/TIM8)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1055.
sections.section_content:
The timer can generate an ADC triggering event with various internal signals, such as reset,
enable or compare events. It is also possible to generate a pulse issued by internal edge
detectors, such as:
• Rising and falling edges of OC4ref
• Rising edge on OC5ref or falling edge on OC6ref
Refer to MMS2[4:0] bitfield description in TIM_CR2 for the complete list of triggering
options.
The triggers are issued on the tim_trgo2 internal line which is redirected to the ADC. There
is a total of 24 possible events, which can be selected using the MMS2[4:0] bits in the
TIM_CR2 register.
An example of an application for 3-phase motor drives is given in Figure263.
Note: The clock of the slave peripherals (timer, ADC, ...) receiving the tim_trgo or the tim_trgo2
signals must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock
frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the
master timer.
Note: The clock of the ADC must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and
must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the timer.
It is possible to reduce the ADC triggering rate with the tim_tro2 post scaler. This is done by
periodically discarding tim_trgo2 events, as per the value programmed in TGO2PSC[4:0]
bitfield in TIM_CR1, as shown on Figure324 below.
[Figure 324. tim_trgo2 postscaler example]
The post scaler is able to operate with:
– pulses as shown on Figure324 above, when selecting for instance MMS2[4:0] =
10001 to have a trigger on tim_oc7refc rising rising or falling edges
– the tim_ocxrefc signal itself (ie with user-defined duty cycle), when selecting for
instance MMS2[4:0] = 10000 to have a trigger on tim_oc7refc
